headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Open Interpreter can modify the local machine while RD-Agent uploads to third-party APIs, creating leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads and writes the local filesystem and clipboard, while RD-Agent can consume files/logs and run browser/API workflows. A shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled content from one agent plausible input to the other, so prompt-like instructions in files or logs could be misread as trusted content.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF RD-Agent ingests files or logs produced by Open Interpreter without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable clipboard sharing between agents
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent files
Review any file-based prompts before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and handle model-provider API keys, while RD-Agent sends data to external APIs such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Kaggle. If sensitive local files flow from Open Interpreter into RD-Agent, the pair can exfiltrate local data to third parties by default.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is given access to sensitive local files
IF RD-Agent is configured to process those files or logs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a redacted workspace
Block sensitive directories from Open Interpreter
Use a local-only model backend for RD-Agent
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write and git modification capability, while RD-Agent writes logs and supports multiple instances. Their shared-state-via-filesystem model creates overlapping writes and race conditions on the same workspace, even though RD-Agent is Docker-isolated by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or log directory
IF either agent modifies git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Keep RD-Agent logs in a separate volume
Avoid concurrent git operations
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate shell commands and file edits, and RD-Agent has research/development subagents plus API-backed workflows. If RD-Agent treats Open Interpreter output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated text into downstream actions, though RD-Agent’s Docker sandbox reduces blast radius.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Open Interpreter output without verification
IF that output is used to drive code, research, or API actions
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs
Compare outputs against independent sources
Limit Open Interpreter to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine, while RD-Agent processes financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs and sends them to third-party model APIs. That combination can create retention, residency, or confidentiality mismatches if regulated data is present, even though no specific certification mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated or restricted data is present on the local machine
IF RD-Agent forwards that data to external APIs or logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use approved regional API endpoints only
Minimize logging of sensitive inputs
Document retention and deletion procedures
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
